addedPassportRecords.coreIdea: Describe electrons, positrons and photons using a charged Dirac field coupled to an Abelian gauge potential.
addedPassportRecords.degreesOfFreedom: Dirac spinor matter and a U(1) gauge field; gauge redundancy must be handled when computing physical amplitudes.
assumptions: One Dirac species in the displayed representative; hbar=c=1.
Metric (+---), D_mu=partial_mu+i e A_mu; F_mu nu=partial_mu A_nu-partial_nu A_mu.
The linked propagator is free and time-ordered; interacting amplitudes require additional calculation.
Modern notation follows Tong; historical primary papers support the perturbative formulation.
addedPassportRecords.mathematicalStructure: L=-F_mu nu F^mu nu/4+psi-bar(i gamma^mu D_mu-m)psi. S_F(p)=i(slash p+m)/(p²-m²+i epsilon), epsilon→0+, with Fourier kernel exp(-ip·(x-y)) and measure d⁴p/(2pi)⁴.
addedPassportRecords.regime: Relativistic electromagnetic calculations with specified particle content, boundary conditions and approximation order.
predictionsConsequences: Perturbative amplitudes organize photon exchange and radiative corrections.
Equivalent historical formulations agree within their shared applicability domain.
addedPassportRecords.evidenceSummary: Formal source review only; precision experiments need separate, source-specific Evidence records.
addedPassportRecords.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: Neither the action nor the historical equivalence proof establishes convergent all-order expansions or an all-energy completion.
limitations: A free propagator is not an exact interacting two-point function.
Gauge-invariant action alone does not supply gauge-fixed amplitudes or renormalized predictions.
The reviewed historical papers do not establish every modern strong-field or nonperturbative claim.
usefulDiscriminators: Against the free Dirac model: calculate the effect of photon exchange and radiative corrections for the same observable.
Against Yang–Mills: compare Abelian versus non-Abelian connection algebra; this is a structural distinction, not an empirical exclusion.
Compare calculations at matched conventions, approximation order and observable definitions.
unresolvedQuestions: Which source-specific precision results should be added as experimental Evidence?
Which controlled approximation is appropriate for a selected interacting observable?

addedPassportRecords.entityType: generator characterization theorem and dynamical framework
addedPassportRecords.scientificStatus: proved under stated semigroup assumptions; physical applicability is model-dependent
addedPassportRecords.coreIdea: Characterize generators of completely positive, trace-preserving continuous quantum dynamical semigroups.
addedPassportRecords.degreesOfFreedom: Density matrices on an N-dimensional Hilbert space; Lindblad also treats normal maps on bounded operators B(Hilbert space), subject to norm continuity.
assumptions: Complete positivity and trace preservation; positivity alone is insufficient.
GKS: finite N. Lindblad: bounded generator, bounded Hamiltonian and jump operators with bounded sum of V†V.
addedPassportRecords.mathematicalStructure: GKS Theorem 2.2, Eq. (2.3), uses a positive coefficient matrix in a traceless orthonormal operator basis. Lindblad Theorem 2, Eqs. (4.2)–(4.3), gives dual Heisenberg/Schrödinger generators. Catalog translation: V_k=sqrt(gamma_k)L_k, gamma_k>=0; H_paper=H_catalog/hbar.
addedPassportRecords.regime: Finite-level semigroup dynamics, or the bounded-generator extension; applying it to a reservoir requires separate justification.
predictionsConsequences: The generator yields CPTP evolution for every nonnegative time.
Its specified coefficients determine relaxation and coherence evolution; the theorem does not supply those coefficients.
addedPassportRecords.evidenceSummary: Mathematical characterization, not an experimental validation of any particular environment or fitted rate.
addedPassportRecords.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: Neither a unique microscopic bath nor a universal memoryless description follows from the generator form.
limitations: General unbounded generators require domain analysis beyond the reviewed theorem.
Time-dependent generators are not automatically time-homogeneous semigroups.
A physical reduced evolution can retain memory; a semigroup approximation needs a justified time window.
usefulDiscriminators: Against general open-system models: test the semigroup composition law on reconstructed maps.
Against memory-dependent models: compare predictions across preparation histories and times outside the fitted interval.
Check complete positivity, not merely positivity on isolated-system states.
unresolvedQuestions: For a chosen system, over which time window is semigroup modeling accurate?
Which generator parameters are identifiable from the available measurements?

after.name: QED Lagrangian
after.plain: L_QED = -F_mn F^mn/4 + psi-bar(i gamma^mu D_mu - m)psi
after.description: Gauge-invariant spinor QED Lagrangian in natural units before gauge fixing.
assumptions: One Dirac matter field coupled minimally to an Abelian U(1) gauge field in the displayed representative.
Natural units hbar=c=1; D_mu psi = (partial_mu + i e A_mu)psi and F_mu nu = partial_mu A_nu - partial_nu A_mu.
Gauge-fixing and ghost terms are absent from the displayed gauge-invariant classical Lagrangian; perturbative quantization requires a gauge choice.
The compact modern notation is source-locked to Tong's course notes rather than attributed verbatim to the 1949 Feynman/Dyson papers.
after.regime: Relativistic spinor quantum electrodynamics in the standard U(1) formulation. The displayed action defines the theory but does not by itself solve strong-field, bound-state or nonperturbative observables.
after.units: Natural units hbar=c=1; restore constants only after choosing a consistent unit convention for both matter and gauge terms.

after.name: GKSL/Lindblad master equation
after.description: Schrödinger-picture GKSL generator for a norm-continuous completely positive trace-preserving quantum dynamical semigroup, with positive rates shown explicitly.
assumptions: Time-homogeneous quantum dynamical semigroup (Markovian semigroup) rather than general non-Markovian evolution.
Bounded/norm-continuous generator in Lindblad's theorem; finite-dimensional systems satisfy the boundedness condition automatically.
gamma_k >= 0; factors sqrt(gamma_k) can equivalently be absorbed into Lindblad operators.
Trace preservation is encoded by the anticommutator terms and complete positivity by the GKSL structure.
Original-paper Hamiltonian equals H/hbar; V_k=sqrt(gamma_k)L_k. Lindblad requires bounded V_k and bounded sum V_k†V_k.
after.regime: Uniformly/norm-continuous CPTP semigroup dynamics. Time-dependent, memory-kernel and general non-Markovian equations are outside the theorem's semigroup scope.
after.units: H has energy units; gamma_k has inverse-time units if L_k is dimensionless; hbar is displayed explicitly in the Hamiltonian term.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical Schrödinger-picture form equivalent to the bounded-generator GKSL theorem
